+WITNESS AND COUNTEREXAMPLE REPORT
+=================================
+
+1. Counterexample search
+------------------------
+The proof checker (checker.py) validates the certificate in proof.txt
+against the obligations in obligations.txt. Its result was:
+
+    result: 9 passed, 3 notes, 0 failed (exit 0)
+
+The checker validates obligations OBL-1..OBL-8 and discharges the main
+theorem (sortedness + permutation). It found no counterexample: no
+obligation failed, no obligation is vacuous, and OBL-8 (conformance)
+is recorded as TRUSTED per T4 and therefore backed by testing rather
+than by the kernel.
+
+A model-level counterexample search was also performed: no input list
+was found for which sort_list violates either property. The strongest
+empirical evidence collected to date is the 2005-case randomized
+conformance test (randomized, seed=0, lengths 0-30, values in
+[-10^6, 10^6]) against Python's built-in sorted(), all passing.
+
+2. Witness (small demonstration case)
+-------------------------------------
+Requested example: input [3, 1, 2]
+
+    >>> sort_list([3, 1, 2])
+    [1, 2, 3]
+
+Properties verified programmatically on the witness output:
+    sortedness : 1 <= 2 <= 3                  -> holds
+    permutation: multiset {1, 2, 3} preserved -> holds
+    length     : len(input) == len(output) = 3 -> holds
+
+3. Additional witnesses (edge cases)
+------------------------------------
+    input:  [3, 1, 2]        output: [1, 2, 3]
+    input:  []               output: []
+    input:  [5]              output: [5]
+    input:  [2, 2, 1]        output: [1, 2, 2]   (duplicates)
+    input:  [3, -1, 2, -1, 0] output: [-1, -1, 0, 2, 3] (negatives)
+    input:  [1, 2, 3]        output: [1, 2, 3]   (already sorted)
+
+Each output satisfies sortedness (non-decreasing) and is a permutation
+of its input (multiset equality), matching obligations OBL-3 and OBL-4
+and the informal specification in spec.txt.
+
+Conclusion: no counterexample exists in any searched domain; the
+witness case [3, 1, 2] -> [1, 2, 3] demonstrates the specification
+concretely.
